newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CADES says to issue 12 bln Ffr 2005 bonds.
newsitem.headline: French CADES says to issue 12 bln Ffr 2005 bonds.

text.p: French welfare debt repayment fund CADES said in a statement on Wednesday it plans to issue 12 billion francs of July 25, 2005 bonds, lead managed by Banque Nationale de Paris and Caisse Nationale du Credit Agricole.
A source close to CADES said the issue "should be this week" and that the fund was not planning to issue either the 2002 or 2007 bond at the same time.

While banking sources in Paris had widely expected CADES to issue a new 2005 bond this week, most had expected a total sale of up to 18 billion francs, including more of either its 2002 or 2007 bonds.
CADES first sold French franc bonds on May 28. It sold 14 billion francs of 2002 bonds and 11 billion francs of 2007 bonds, both priced at seven basis points over government bonds.

Traders said on Tuesday there was a good chance the next CADES issue would be priced at six basis points over government bonds, given how well the 2002 and 2007 bonds were trading in the secondary market.
